messages:
maria-support: heads up — enterprise customer hit a production bug: tool-call args arriving via streaming are being cut mid-JSON when routed through their edge LB. They see valid SSE events but the final JSON object for the tool args is truncated, causing schema validation failures on our side. request_id=rid_9a8b7c logs attached by customer.

irina-support: customer repro steps: they stream a long tool args payload (large nested JSON) using server-sent events, proxy is an internal ALB that does chunk coalescing. when it truncates we get something like: 

maria-support (quote):
```
data: {"tool": "charge_customer", "args": {"invoice_id": "inv_12345", "items": [ ... huge array ... ], "metadata": {"note": "..." }  // <-- stream ends here, missing closing } }

// our server throws: JSON parse error: unexpected end of input
```

sanjay-sre: can you paste the raw SSE payload (including chunk boundaries) and any edge logs? I want to check if the LB is splitting on multibyte boundaries or closing connection early.

irina-support: pasted raw sample from customer below (they redacted sensitive fields):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

7a
: ping

3f
data: {"tool":"charge_customer","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_12345","items":[{"id":"sku_1","qty":1}, {"id":"sku_2","qty":2}],"metadata":{"notes":"long note...

25
...continues here but then stops mid-char
0

```

lina-eng-runtime: interesting — the LB sends chunk sizes but the app server consumes streaming frames as they arrive and immediately forwards SSE to our toolcall parser. If a chunk ends inside a multibyte UTF-8 sequence or mid-escape, the concatenated buffer can be invalid until the next chunk arrives. Ideally parser should reassemble until it sees a complete JSON object before validation.

tom-eng-api: quick questions: 1) is this reproducible internally? 2) which SDK/language did they use to produce the stream? details matter (node fetch vs curl vs python).

irina-support: customer says this happens only through their ALB path. Direct traffic to our hosted API does not reproduce. They used Node fetch on their side and also observed it with their Java-based proxy. They can reproduce reliably by pushing a big nested args JSON > 16KB.

maria-support: customer supplied a trace id: rid_9a8b7c, and edge logs show an upstream reset at 14:23:07Z. Their LB logs show chunk flushes at odd offsets.

sanjay-sre: repro plan — I can spin up a small ALB-like proxy locally and try to stream a long JSON with SSE. If I see mid-chunk boundary splits that create invalid UTF-8 or truncated tokens we should add a server-side reassembly buffer for SSE toolcall messages. Also need to rule out our nginx side sendfile/fastcgi buffering.

lina-eng-runtime: temporary mitigations we can offer customer: 1) set their LB to disable HTTP response buffering/flush frequency (if supported), 2) switch to websocket (binary-safe), or 3) append a sentinel newline or length-prefix in the SSE payload so we can treat arg frames as length-delimited instead of relying on chunk boundaries.

tom-eng-api: patch suggestion from runtime: change toolcall streaming path to accumulate 'data:' lines until a blank line ends the event, then attempt JSON parse; do not attempt parsing mid-event. This will be a small change in the SSE handler — reassemble event payload before handing to schema validator. Should be low-risk. Lina, can you estimate?

lina-eng-runtime: estimate: ~1.5d to implement + unit tests + QA. I'll turn into a small PR and include a toggle so we can enable server-side reassembly only for streaming toolcall endpoints.

maria-support: customer asked for a timeline. We told them we can provide a hotfix to our hosted endpoint in ~48 hours and a workaround guide now. They prefer a configuration change on their LB if possible.

sanjay-sre: additional ask — can we add defensive logging so when JSON parse fails we log the raw event ASCII hex snippet (redact PII) and the request_id. That will help correlate with customer chunks. Low-risk.

lina-eng-runtime: agree. I'll add debug-level logging behind a feature flag. We'll also document the 'length-prefix' pattern for SSE tool args in our API docs as a suggested compatibility mode.

irina-support: creating a KB note for customer with repro steps and the following temporary curl example they can use to test after LB changes: 

```bash
# stream a length-prefixed JSON event to our test endpoint
echo -e "event: toolcall\ndata: 8192\ndata: {\"tool\":\"charge_customer\",\"args\":{...}}\n\n" | curl -v -H "Content-Type: text/event-stream" --no-buffer --data-binary @- https://api.redwood-inference.test/stream
```

maria-support: deploy-bot: can we schedule a canary deploy for the reassembly fix behind a flag? :deploy-bot:

deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: canary group=10% service=runtime-sse reassembly-guard=true window=0400-0600 UTC

tom-eng-api: once PR is up ping me. Also add an integration test that simulates chunked boundaries splitting inside strings and multibyte utf8.

maria-support: customer happy with plan and temporary docs. I'll keep this thread updated and post final patch link when merged. :thumbsup:

sanjay-sre: follow-up note — consider adding an event-level CRC or simple checksum in the SSE metadata for the longer term so replays / partial receives can be detected by both sides. Worth a design doc if we see this again across customers. :eyes:

lina-eng-runtime: noted for post-mortem. I'll open a design ticket and link it here after the hotfix PR.

maria-support: thanks everyone — closing internal loop, will update the customer after canary completes.
